svg.text: The LMAX Disruptor feeding a CLOB
BTC-USD ≈ $79,000 · consumed events built the book · published events wait · the claimed event is next
claim the next slot → write the order into it, in place → publish by advancing the cursor — never blocks unless the ring is full
Ring buffer — 65,536 pre-allocated slots, reused forever

g.text: free — consumed and reused, never freed

svg.text: Slots show the last three digits of the 64-bit sequence — 8.2M events in, the
ring is on lap ~125,600. With N a power of two, seq & (N-1) is seq mod N
Published events — drained strictly in sequence, by ONE thread
joins the best-ask FIFO, 4th in line
still being written — crosses the spread
Single-writer matching core — the BTC-USD limit order book
time priority (FIFO) — the seq tags under the best ask are its arrival order
when …427 drains, the match is fully determined by price-time priority:
it crosses the spread at the best ask — fills the 0.30 (seq …398) whole, then 0.70 of the 0.85 (seq …402); 0.15 of …402 rests.
It never reaches 78,997.50 — whose lone 1.05 dies to the cancel queued at …423 anyway.
The book is a fold over the event log — determinism is what makes replay-recovery (and lmax-bench’s cross-language checksum) possible.
In the benchmark the same book runs on integer ticks; each event carries (kind, side, price, qty, id). BTC-USD priced August 2026.
